title: Invoiced values inconsistent with the goods or services delivered
definition: Invoice values that depart materially from what comparable trade would cost — the goods over-invoiced and the payments under-invoiced, or the reverse — with no commercial reason offered. The indicator measures the divergence between the declared value and the market value of the trade.
evidence_to_cite: the invoice, the contract and the payment record, each cited by its own source id
the independent evidence of the market value relied on
the customs or tax documentation, where the trade crossed a border
benign_explanations: A long-standing relationship between related parties priced on a cost-plus basis.
A market with few comparable trades, so the benchmark is weak.
A genuine change in price, quantity or quality between the compared periods.
Freight, insurance and tax included in one invoice and excluded from the other.

sources.citation: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, trade-based money laundering guidance, summarised in the FinCrime regulatory index.

notes: A comparison needs a comparison class. Without one, the divergence is an opinion, and the record has to say which class was used.
